pins.name: D0
pins.label: GPIO0 (Button)
pins.notes: PIN_BUTTON1 / board.BUTTON1 — onboard tactile button (also doubles as the UF2/BOOTSEL button per this board's own pins_arduino.h comment "'Boot0' button also on GPIO #0"). Confirmed active-low with internal pull-up via CircuitPython example code (`button.switch_to_input(pull=digitalio.Pull.UP)`) referenced from learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-fruit-jam. Input-only, matching this repo's simple-tactile-button precedent (e.g. pimoroni_explorer SWITCH_A-Z).

pins.name: D20
pins.label: D20 (GPIO20)
pins.notes: Main I2C0 SDA — also the STEMMA QT connector's data line. This same bus additionally reaches the onboard TLV320DAC3100 audio codec (I2C address 0x18, used by the codec's control interface alongside its separate I2S audio-data pins) and, when a display is connected, EDID readout over the DVI port (learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-fruit-jam/i2c-3 confirms all of these appear on one I2C scan). Left general-purpose: this is the board's standard user-facing Wire/STEMMA QT bus, matching this repo's precedent of keeping a shared expansion I2C bus general-purpose even when onboard devices also sit on it.

pins.name: D21

pins.name: D29
pins.label: GPIO29 (Led active low)
pins.notes: PIN_LED / board.LED / LED_BUILTIN — onboard status LED, wired REVERSED from most boards: anode to 3.3V, cathode to GPIO29, so LOW turns it on and HIGH turns it off. Confirmed verbatim via learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-fruit-jam/pinout ("setting the pin to LOW results in the LED turning on... This is unusual and is the reverse from most other boards"). The SAME physical pin is ALSO wired to an onboard IR receiver (silkscreen "IR In", CircuitPython board.IR) per the same source — a confirmed dual-purpose pin. No 'IR receiver' capability exists in this codebase's vocabulary, so digital_input is kept alongside led_low (rather than dropped as on a single-purpose LED pin) to reflect that this pin is a genuine, sourced, general digital-input-capable line as well as an LED output.
